baseline.installDetail: yarn 1.22.19 on Node 16.20.2 placed 713 package directories with --frozen-lockfile holding and lifecycle scripts disabled.
baseline.buildDetail: next build passed the repository's own typecheck (typescript 4.5.5) and compiled through Babel in 8 seconds, emitting 3 static pages: / at 64.6 kB (140 kB first load), /404 at 2.84 kB, /_app shared at 75.8 kB.
baseline.exportDetail: next export wrote 2 HTML documents plus _next/static, _next/data, and the public assets into out/. The static-export path is the migration story for this fixture: upstream's own preview script is bin/graveyard && yarn build && next export && http-server out/.

journeyLimitation.statement: Admitted under the charter's "where the application surface allows it" qualifier. This application has one authored route, no navigation, no form submission, no authentication, no persistence, and no server. It cannot exercise routing, data mutation, session, or multi-page migration behavior, and no result obtained from it may be generalised to Next.js applications with multiple routes, API routes, middleware, or server rendering.

mustBeBlockedByWitnessUnits.when: client-side, unconditional (guarded only by typeof window)

mustBeBlockedByWitnessUnits.warning: must fail fast rather than hang; the authored onerror path renders a local fallback, but a stalled request will outlast the 5-second expect timeout

thirdPartyEgress.note: The ad <li> exists whether or not the ad script loads, so both upstream count assertions hold offline.

assetExclusions.policy: Third-party marks carried inside the immutable archive only. Not to be extracted, re-hosted, re-encoded, thumbnailed, or reused as Versionless assets, and not to appear legibly in any published capture. They sit in the footer, below the journey surface, so this constrains nothing the journeys need.

knownRisks: One authored route. This fixture's evidentiary reach is narrow by construction; see journeyLimitation.
Both upstream count assertions silently depend on a non-data <li> ad slot being present. Any later work that removes or conditionally renders that slot changes the expected counts by one.
The filter spec selects its option by nth-child position inside react-select's internal listbox DOM, so it is coupled to react-select 5.2.2 internals rather than to a label.

A production build reaches three third-party script hosts, two of which only appear in production. A witness that builds for production and forgets to block them will observe network flake that has nothing to do with the migration under test.
lodash is imported by components/Carbon.tsx without being a declared dependency; it works today only because a transitive copy is hoisted to the root of node_modules.

The upstream Playwright workflow runs against a deployed Netlify preview URL, not a local server, and playwright.config.ts has its webServer block commented out. Any local witness run must supply its own server and base URL.
graveyard.json names third-party products and links to third-party articles. It is public commentary data, not Versionless content, and must not be edited to suit a test.

priorArtifactSeparation.statement: A retired-goal artifact for the same upstream pin exists under the old slug and was ruled not grandfathered. It was not touched, reused, or extended. This fixture stands on its own acquisition; the retired record was read read-only for an independent cross-check, which agreed on every immutable fact.

nonclaims: This fixture record fixes an identity, records the cell in which a baseline ran, and describes an application surface. It establishes no browser behavior, no journey pass, no migration feasibility, no pilot status, no production readiness, no certification, and no legal approval.
No adapter, transform, or migration lane is declared for this fixture by the unit that ingested it.
